In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493, 2498,
2499, 2503, 2505, 2507, 2512, 2519, 2521, 2530, and 2534, due to the continuing state of emergency, including
masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being
broadcast via teleconference. Members of the public may participate virtually in the meeting in the following
ways:

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 9128) from any phone, Meeting ID:
867 8530 7395 Passcode: 900177. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call in option from
a phone line.)

- Public correspondence may be emailed to the rosap@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m.
prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the Park and Activities Commission for their consideration
and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an
"eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp
page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen
by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by
entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 867 8530 7395 Passcode: 900177.

- Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the agenda you
would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are available on
the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING
  December 19, 2022

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  A regular meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates
  was called to order at 7:02 p.m. via teleconference, by CHAIR CIAROLLA.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR CIAROLLA led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Pope, Ciarolla, Romanelli, Persichina, Bain, and
  Retz (joined at 7:11 pm)

  Commissioners Absent:  McCormick

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF
  NOVEMBER 14, 2022

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR BAIN
  to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  November 14, 2022.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  NEW PROGRAM PROPOSAL – SILVER SPUR LITTLE LEAGUE

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
December 19, 2022
   Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the new program
  proposal for a Silver Spur Little League winter break camp.

  CHAIR CIAROLLA asked Mr. Richard Blanch, the Silver Spur Little League (SSLL)
  representative present at the meeting, to speak to the Commission regarding the
  proposed Silver Spur Little League winter baseball academy camp.

  Mr. Blanch presented his organization’s proposal for the new winter baseball
  academy camp at Ernie Howlett Park.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ joined the meeting at 7:11 pm.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI expressed concern about meeting to make a
  decision about the new program without the proper vetting. He stated that he was
  not sure if this proposed winter baseball academy fell under the current guidelines
  in the SSLL contract. He inquired about the camp fee, the camp costs, the allocation
  of funds generated as SSLL is a non-profit organization, and the potential need for
  business licensing. He stated that in order to address this opportunity properly the
  Youth Sports Subcommittee should have time to look over all details of the
  proposed program prior to the Commission making a final decision. He also stated
  that this program seemed like a great opportunity for the youth of the community
  who love the game of baseball, which would provide the opportunity to learn new
  skills from former professional baseball players. He reiterated concern about the
  urgency of a decision regarding the program without going through the proper
  process that is typically required to make a decision regarding a new activity.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN stated that she is in favor of having youth sports camps available
  to the community when children are on break from school. She asked how SSLL
  requested the new program that is outside of their standard terms of the
  organization’s contract and whether maintenance of the park or the community
  would be negatively impacted by the new use of the field during the time requested.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that she is also in support of youth sports camps
  during school breaks. She also stated that she agreed with COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI regarding the urgency of making a decision about the proposed
  program and having an opportunity to have more time to review the program prior
  to making a final decision.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ stated that he is also very much in support of youth sports
  in the community. He stated that his main concern was that there did not appear to
  be proper procedures in place to advise staff on how to evaluate new program
  proposals. He also stated that the Youth Sports Subcommittee should come up with
  proper procedures to create a fair system to all community members and

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
December 19, 2022
   organizations for staff and the Commission to properly make formal decisions
  regarding these new program proposals. Assistant City Manager Davis stated that
  the challenge that staff had regarding this proposed program was that there were
  no proper procedures in place for the fast turnaround needed for the SSLL proposal
  and that was one of the main reasons why the meeting was held that night. She
  also stated that staff would be working with the Youth Sports Subcommittee to draft
  a policy to address these issues in the future.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA stated that this was a good time to figure out how
  to establish the proper guidelines as this will be an issue for staff regarding all
  organizations using City parks not just Little League.

  CHAIR CIAROLLA asked Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith whether this
  program would impact the scheduled maintenance of the fields. Maintenance
  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that there was typically no scheduled field
  maintenance during the winter months.

  CHAIR CIAROLLA stated that during her time on the Commission she has noticed
  that the Silver Spur Little League organization typically states that they do not
  properly understand the procedures. She also expanded that she agreed that there
  should be standard procedures in place to help clarify processes to organizations.
  ACM Davis stated that there is typically a leadership change every few years with
  the SSLL board of directors which offers a challenge to both the organization and
  staff. She also stated that the new board is excited about reenergizing the league,
  so staff is reminding them of the proper protocols and procedures. She added that
  staff will be working with the Youth Sports Subcommittee very soon to create a
  formal policy for all organizations to be passed to SSLL leadership for a better
  understanding of the protocols and procedures.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN asked if there was a way to meet with the Youth Sports
  Subcommittee to review this program prior to having the Commission make a final
  decision. ACM Davis stated that the Subcommittee typically looks over the
  concerns and issues and then the Commission makes the final decision, but staff
  felt that there was not enough time to meet with the Subcommittee regarding the
  program proposal and publish the agenda for this meeting.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA stated that it was a difficult time to try and rush this
  issue and that the Commission should really take its time.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ stated that something needs to be in place to create the
  proper procedures for all organizations to follow and that it is still premature and
  that there is not enough time to make a formal decision.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
December 19, 2022
   CHAIR CIAROLLA asked whether the Commission would approve or disapprove
  the presented program proposal. COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA stated that this
  proposal should go back to the Youth Sports Subcommittee before a final decision
  can be made adding that it should be discussed, and the proper protocol and
  procedures followed.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN asked which Commissioners are members of the Youth Sports
  Subcommittee. COMISSIONERS POPE, ROMANELLI and PERSICHINA
  acknowledged that they are the current members.

  ACM Davis stated that the typical process is for the proposal to go to the Youth
  Sports Subcommittee and then to the Commission for final approval. She also
  stated that staff could go through this process, but there would not be enough time
  for final approval for this current proposed SSLL winter baseball academy program.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion to:

  HAVE THE YOUTH SPORTS SUBCOMMITTEE STUDY THE ISSUE OF
  WHICH ORGANIZATIONS CAN REQUEST A PERMIT, TO CONSIDER
  UNDER WHAT CIRCUMSTANCES THEY CAN REQUEST A PERMIT,
  TIMING, AND NOTICING PROCEDURES, TO PROVIDE GUIDELINES TO
  STAFF; TABLE THE REQUEST BY SSLL UNTIL THE YOUTH SPORTS
  SUBCOMMITEE HAS TIME TO ESTABLISH A POLICY THAT CAN BE
  APPROVED BY THE COMMISSION.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI amended the motion to include:

  RECEIVE INPUT FROM THE CITY ATTORNEY AND ADD A BUSINESS
  LICENSE REVIEW TO THE PROCESS IF NEEDED.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN further amended the motion to include:

  DETERMINE IF AN AMENDMENT SHOULD BE MADE TO THE SSLL
  CONTRACT FOR PROGRAMMING THAT FALLS OUTSIDE THE SCOPE
  OF THE CONTRACT AND HAVE THE AMENDMENT PUT IN PLACE
  PRIOR TO ANY ADVERTISING OF THAT PROGRAMMING.

  The amended motion was seconded by COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA.

  In response to COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA’S question, ACM Davis affirmed
  that the program would not be moving forward based on the motion.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
December 19, 2022
   7.  STAFF ITEMS

  NONE.

  8.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR CIAROLLA MOVED TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  ADJOURN THE MEETING AT 7:33 PM TO THE NEXT PARK AND ACTIVITIES
  COMMISSION MEETING ON JANUARY 17, 2023, AT 7:00 P.M., WHICH WILL BE
  HELD AT THE CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBER.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
